overview.heading: What is Bachelor of Radiology & Imaging Technology?
paragraphs: Bachelor of Radiology & Imaging Technology is an undergraduate health-sciences course that trains students to assist in medical diagnosis through imaging. The work centres on operating and checking machines used for X-rays, CT scans, MRI scans and related tests, while also helping with correct patient positioning, image quality and radiation safety. It is a practical course, and much of the learning takes place in labs and hospital settings.

Students usually study anatomy, physiology, radiographic techniques, imaging physics and radiation protection. They also learn how to prepare patients, follow safety rules, work with doctors and technologists, and support the smooth running of an imaging department. Because the job involves real equipment and real patients, steady hands, attention to detail and calm communication matter as much as classroom knowledge.

After graduation, students can start as radiology or imaging technologists in hospitals, diagnostic centres and clinics. Pay depends on the city, employer, shift pattern, experience and the type of imaging work handled. Someone starting in general X-ray may earn less than a technologist who later moves into CT, MRI, emergency imaging or other specialised roles, so one salary figure cannot describe every graduate.

snapshot.data_note: Pay in this field changes with city, hospital type, shift duties, experience and the imaging area handled. Entry roles are usually in general radiography, while higher earnings are more common after moving into CT, MRI, emergency or other specialised work.

salary.note: A common entry-level range is about INR 250000 to INR 450000 a year, while a broader India range for radiologic technologists runs from about INR 30000 to INR 800000 a year. Experience, specialisation and location can move pay well above or below the middle.

caution.heading: Things students should know before choosing this course
points: The job is not limited to pressing buttons; safe patient handling, positioning and image quality are part of daily work.
Busy hospitals can mean long shifts, night duty and emergency cases.
Specialised roles such as CT, MRI or nuclear medicine usually need extra skill-building after the degree.
Students who dislike close contact with patients or strict safety routines may find this field uncomfortable.

curriculum.assessment_methods: Continuous internal assessment through class tests, practical records, lab demonstrations, viva voce, clinical logbooks, hospital rotation performance, semester-end written exams, and final project or dissertation evaluation in the last year.
curriculum.learning_activities: Classroom teaching, imaging lab practice, hospital and diagnostic-centre rotations, supervised patient positioning practice, machine handling demonstrations, case discussions, report observation, simulation exercises, and project work.

faqs.answer: This course trains students to help operate imaging equipment such as X-ray, CT, MRI, and related diagnostic systems under clinical supervision. Graduates usually work in hospitals, diagnostic centres, and imaging departments.
faqs.question: What does a radiology and imaging technology graduate do?

faqs.answer: Most colleges ask for Class 12 Science. Biology and Physics are usually the key subjects, and some colleges also look at Chemistry and minimum marks in Class 12.
faqs.question: What should students study in Class 12 to be eligible?

faqs.answer: The usual duration is 3 to 4 years, depending on the university and the structure of the programme. Some colleges include a clinical internship or rotation in the final part of the course.
faqs.question: How long does the course take?

faqs.answer: This is a hands-on course. Students spend time in labs, imaging departments, and supervised clinical settings, so comfort with equipment, patient handling, and shift-based work matters.
faqs.question: Is the course mostly theory or practical?

faqs.answer: In India, the imaging technologist role is generally not a separate medical licence role like a doctor’s specialty. After graduation, students usually join hospital or diagnostic-centre jobs and may need employer training, and for higher responsibility they often add certification, experience, or a postgraduate course.
faqs.question: What comes after graduation before working in the field?

faqs.answer: Fees vary widely across India, but a common annual range for this kind of private undergraduate health-science course is about INR 50000 to INR 250000. Government or aided colleges can be lower, and many private colleges are higher.
faqs.question: How much can the course cost?

parent_corner.intro: Bachelor of Radiology & Imaging Technology suits students who enjoy biology, physics, and applied science, and who are comfortable in a hospital setting. It is a practical undergraduate path into diagnostic imaging support, not a desk-based degree. Families should check whether the college has good lab equipment, real clinical posting arrangements, and clear internship support. A child choosing this course should be ready for patient contact, discipline, and shift-style work later on. It also helps to ask how much of the programme is classroom learning versus supervised practice, because that balance shapes job readiness. For many families, the main questions are about safety, future study options, and whether the college has strong hospital exposure.
